title: Fallback variant compatibility playbook and ongoing maintenance for routing
creator: Lena Chen
description: Create and maintain a practical playbook and automation suite that ensures fallback model variants used by smart routing remain behaviorally compatible with primary models. Scope: tokenizer behavior (byte-level/tokenization differences), effective context window equivalence, KV cache interchangeability, structured output / function-calling parity, and downstream tooling compatibility (embeddings/reranking). Outcome: predictable fallbacks with measurable regression detection and clear remediation runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix updated to include tokenizer version, max context, kv-cache format and supported tooling flags for all active variants
Automated parity tests added to CI: tokenizer roundtrip, context-slice consistency, kv-forward/backward compatibility tests
Regression alerts wired into Console for fallback-induced quality drops (prompt-set baselining & alert thresholds)
Playbook published (internal Confluence) with rollout and rollback steps, plus runbook links for on-call
At least one canary rollout of fallback-enabled routing exercised across regions and tiers without user-visible regressions
tasks: Inventory current fallback variants and collect metadata (tokenizer version, max_seq, kv-format, tool_flags)
Design tokenizer roundtrip harness and add deterministic seeds for CI
Implement kv-cache interchange test between primary and fallback variants
Add structured-output/function-call smoke tests for fallback compatibility
Create dashboard: per-route fallback rate, regression test pass rate, quality delta on eval prompt sets
Author playbook: decision criteria for allowing a variant as fallback, rollback procedures, communication checklist
Coordinate with Model Onboarding to require compatibility metadata for new variants

risks: Late discovery of tokenizer differences causing subtle prompt meaning changes
KV-cache schema divergence requiring coordinated model rebuilds
Coverage gaps in eval prompt-sets that miss domain-specific regressions
Cross-region rollout complexity: variant availability differs between regions and may mask issues
